tc.research_text.ARCANEASSEMBLER: Materials arranged from the record, vis supplied according to the recipe: the chamber completed the work that used to keep me at the bench.
tc.research_text.ARCANEASSEMBLER.stage.1:
The molecular assembler arranges the materials accurately enough, yet the arcane recipe produces nothing. It still lacks a sceptre to guide the vis.
I have chosen a silverwood sceptre, charged it fully, and prepared it for infusion with the assembler. The sceptre will become part of the machine; I cannot expect to retrieve it afterwards.
tc.research_text.ARCANEASSEMBLER.stage.2:
I recorded the first recipe in a knowledge core and placed it in the chamber. Once the Vis Relay Interface was connected, the machine finally produced the result. It needs both the record and the vis.
Acceleration Cards work as well. My timing notes read 20 ticks without cards, 4 ticks less per card, at most 4 cards, and 4 ticks with all slots filled.
Armour with a vis discount also reduces consumption when placed in the equipment slots. The spare set need not spend all its time on a stand.
tc.research_text.ARCANECRAFTINGTERMINAL: The workbench can draw its materials from the network and return the finished item to storage. There is no longer a reason to walk between two benches.
Half a recipe is forever sitting on the arcane workbench while the missing piece is in the network. I have tried joining the workbench to a terminal so that recipe and stock can be seen together.
With the materials arranged, the wand still recognises the recipe. There is room left for armour slots, which should spare me putting a whole set into my pack each time I change.

With the wand in its slot and the materials arranged, the terminal displays the vis required. I checked it with crystals and with a wand; the costs are worked out before the result is taken.
The ME network pays for untyped aura by default. After I fitted a Vis Connection Card and repeated the recipe, that part was drawn from around the terminal instead. The card deserves a page of its own.
tc.research_text.BASEENERGISTICS:
Another row of jars has appeared beside the workbench. Some are empty, others hold only a trace of essentia, yet none of the labels can come off.
An ME network can hold an item in a quartz cell and return it intact. What would a formation core or annihilation core make of essentia?
I have set aside two matching jars: one for comparison, one to connect to the core. I will begin with an aspect I can readily recognise.
Textures for newer versions by @麦淇淋.
tc.research_text.CERTUS_DUPE:
The core recognises the duplicated Certus Quartz, and circuits made from it behave normally. Its origin does not seem to matter to the network.
When the supply runs low, I can prepare the essentia for this alchemical recipe instead.
tc.research_text.DIGISENTIA: The jar is empty, but the terminal still has a reading. Reversing the conversion returns the same essentia.
tc.research_text.DIGISENTIA.stage.1:
The first attempt failed. The core could move the jar, but did nothing with its contents. Perhaps the trouble comes before conversion: an item has a fixed form; essentia does not.
I altered the inlet so that a little essentia could disperse in a buffer first. A new reading finally appeared. When I opened the circuit, though, several contacts had discoloured. They will need a coat of quicksilver before the next trial.
tc.research_text.DIGISENTIA.stage.2:
§lDiffusion Core§r
The coating has held. Essentia passing through the buffer becomes stored network contents, and no more is lost when the pipe is disconnected. I have kept this arrangement.§lCondensation Core§r
Reversing the wires is not enough to reverse the process. Dispersed essentia must gather again before it can enter a vessel. After adjusting the buffer, the first phial matched the control sample. The two cores can finally work together.
tc.research_text.DISTILLATIONENCODER:
The thaumic lens can read an item's aspects before it is distilled. I placed items in the lens slot and compared several readings with the actual yield; they agreed.
After selecting the aspect I need, the §lDistillation Encoder§r writes the yield to an encoded pattern. The network then has the record it needs to arrange distillation, without my copying every result by hand.
tc.research_text.ESSENTIACELLWORKBENCH.s:
The cell is not full, yet it will accept no new aspect types. A look at its contents explains why: many aspects are present only in traces, but each still takes a place.
I want to separate the common supplies from these odds and ends. Specifying the permitted aspects before a cell enters the drive should spare me repeated sorting.

Placing the cell in the upper slot and dragging aspects into the partition grid records which types it may accept. Once back in the drive, it no longer collected the other aspects.
A cell already in use need not be copied out slot by slot. Partitioning by its contents fills the grid with the aspects already stored; I only need to check the result.
tc.research_text.ESSENTIALEVELEMITTER: The redstone lamp lit when the supply reached the chosen level. Letting that signal control the equipment beats repeatedly checking the terminal.
tc.research_text.ALCHEMYPROVIDER: As the vessel uses essentia, the network replenishes it. Each aspect need not have its own bus.
tc.research_text.ALCHEMYPROVIDER.connect:
Extending the connection to another bench led to an §lAlchemy Wireless Receiver§r. Bound to a provider, it can feed adjacent vessels at a distance and return their essentia to the network, up to 16 points per transfer. Nothing remains inside when it is removed; it provides the connection rather than storage.
The working range is 32 blocks, with at most 8 receivers per provider. Each adds 5 to the idle power draw. Both distance and network power must be allowed for before placing them.
tc.research_text.ALCHEMYPROVIDER.stage.1:
When feeding alchemical equipment, resetting the export buses is often the tedious part. A change of recipe means checking the aspects again.
The vessel already knows what it will accept. I have tried letting a provider read that demand and draw the corresponding essentia from the network. The pipe connection retains 8 suction, so the existing plumbing need not be abandoned.
tc.research_text.ALCHEMYPROVIDER.stage.2:
With the §lAlchemy Provider§r connected to the network and placed against the vessel, the missing essentia began to return. A different vessel drew a different aspect; no filter had to be set on the provider.
After I withdrew the last of that aspect from the network, replenishment stopped. The vessel's demand alone is not enough; there must be a supply to draw from.
tc.research_text.ALCHEMYPROVIDER.tool.st:
The §lWireless Binding Tool§r remembers the receiver's position. I sneaked and right-clicked the receiver, then did the same at the provider; the connection was made.
A regular right-click on either end shows its position and partner. If binding fails, the tool reports whether the distance is too great or the provider has no room for another receiver. That is easier to trace than a long run of pipes.
tc.research_text.ESSENTIASTORAGE: The essentia in the quartz cell can be recovered. There is finally some room on the jar shelves. The next question is how much a cell will hold.
tc.research_text.ESSENTIASTORAGE16k.stag:
With more components connected, the original control circuit is no longer adequate. I have replaced it with a more capable circuit and adjusted the connections between them.
If it can complete a stable write, the capacity can be raised to 16k.

With the 16k cell installed, continuous distillation no longer fills the drive so quickly. Its byte capacity is sixteen times that of the first cell, and withdrawals work as before.
Some of the jars I kept in reserve can go into storage themselves.
tc.research_text.ESSENTIASTORAGE1k.stage:
An ordinary storage component will not retain the converted essentia. I infused Certus Quartz with concentrated essence and repeated the write. This time, the reading survived the power being cut.
A higher concentration seems to allow more storage, but I am reluctant to infuse too much at once. A small component and repeated deposits and withdrawals should tell me whether the quartz can bear it.

The finished 1k cell is now in the ME drive. After several deposits and withdrawals, the jar and terminal still agree.
Essentia quantity alone does not account for the space used. My notes show 8 points per byte, another 8 bytes for each aspect, and room for at most 63 aspect types. A wider assortment leaves less space for the essentia itself.
tc.research_text.ESSENTIASTORAGE4k.stage:
The first cell filled before distillation was finished. More cells would help, but the drive has only so many slots.
I have connected three 1k components to a common circuit and rearranged their storage structure. This should give me a 4k component.

The new cell does have four times the byte capacity. The old 1k cells remain in the drive and work alongside it.
This time, there was still space left when distillation finished.
tc.research_text.ESSENTIASTORAGE64k.stag:
The next component will hold essentia at a greater density. The circuit can be improved again, but the old casing will not suffice.
I have checked the enclosure and contacts before filling it and withdrawing each aspect in turn. The larger the capacity, the less I want to omit that test.

The 64k cell passed the deposit and withdrawal trials. Its byte capacity is sixty-four times that of the 1k cell, and it shares a drive with the smaller cells.
There is little reason to expand further for now. The aspects present only in traces still deserve their own partitions, lest too many types take up the available slots.
tc.research_text.ESSENTIATERMINAL: Digitised essentia cannot be seen or smelled. There ought to be somewhere to check how much remains.
I compared the terminal readings with each jar until I could account for the network's essentia. With a vessel connected, the amount withdrawn agreed as well. The §lEssentia Terminal§r is ready for regular use.
Watching the display all day is less appealing. I connected an §lEssentia Level Emitter§r, chose an aspect and quantity, and had it signal when the supply rose above or fell below that amount. A distillation setup can use that signal to start or stop.

A monitor beside the equipment saves opening the terminal every time. A wrench unlocks it; a label, jar or phial selects the aspect with a right-click. An empty hand clears the selection, and the wrench locks it again.
The §lConversion Monitor§r also handles deposits and withdrawals. Once locked, right-clicking with a vessel fills it from the network; sneaking and right-clicking deposits its contents instead.
With many vessels to empty, two successive right-clicks while sneaking deposit the essentia from all vessels in the inventory. I should check that I intend to empty them all first.
tc.research_text.ESSENTIAVIBRATIONCHAMBE:
Distilled essentia still holds energy. Rather than feed more fuel into the vibration chamber, I altered its inlet to burn essentia directly.
After the first point was consumed, the energy buffer registered a charge and the network began drawing from it. Another aspect gave a different burn time and output. They cannot all be treated as the same fuel.Pipes and an essentia export bus can both replenish the supply. I kept three readings on the display: essentia remaining, burn progress, and stored energy. They were useful for comparing the trials.
When the buffer filled, the burn stopped and the inlet's suction withdrew. It resumed only after the network drew more energy. At least it should not consume an entire jar when there is no demand.
tc.research_text.FOCUS_AEWRENCH:
Finding a wrench while holding the wand usually means putting something down first. I worked its functions into a focus and tried it on the wand.
Sneaking and left-clicking rotates the equipment; sneaking and right-clicking dismantles it. One fewer tool needs a place on the rack.
tc.research_text.GOLEMWIFI:
After collecting items, the golem always returns to a chest to unload. With the chest far away, it spends more time walking than collecting.
I fitted a wireless connection to a backpack, bound it to the network with a memory card, and gave it to the golem. When it became idle, the items appeared directly in the ME terminal.Transmission stopped beyond the wireless access point's range, and also when the network shut down. Its working area must remain within the signal.
Sneaking and right-clicking with a golem bell removes the pack. Right-clicking with a supported camouflage block changes its appearance. If the golem is to carry it all the time, it may as well match.
tc.research_text.OCCULTMONITOR.stage.1:
Discovering a shortage halfway through an infusion leaves little time to replenish it calmly. I want to see how much the altar can draw before beginning.
The §lOccult Monitor§r counts jars, providers, and network supplies together, displaying requirements and shortages. It also records the item being infused, stability, and risk. At the end of the trial, it gave a redstone pulse.
tc.research_text.OCCULTMONITOR.stage.2:
The monitor needs a network connection, a place within 12 blocks of the altar along each axis, and a Thaumonomicon to interpret the readings.
The display floats above it and can be seen within 8 blocks. I could still read the text from behind a wall. The block tooltip offers the readings as well.
The book is not consumed. Sneaking and right-clicking with an empty hand returns it.
tc.research_text.INFUSIONPROVIDER: The altar drew essentia from the provider, though the provider still read empty. The consumed point had come from the network.
The altar seems unconcerned with the shape of the vessel it draws from. I connected the network's conversion core to an interface that could answer it, supplying just one aspect at first.
The stream appeared, and the network supply fell by one point. The altar can draw directly, but pipes cannot treat this §lInfusion Provider§r as a jar. It has no essentia supply of its own and accepts no deposits.

The space beneath the altar is convenient for wiring, but the provider need not sit there. Anywhere within 12 blocks along each axis will do once connected to the ME network. The altar draws 1 point at a time; idle power draw is 5.
I briefly cut the power, and the stream stopped. Before beginning an infusion, I must check the network's power and essentia as well as the materials.
tc.research_text.KNOWLEDGECORE: After removing the core and returning it to the inscriber, the recipe was still there. This will hold the records the chamber needs.
tc.research_text.KNOWLEDGEINSCRIBER: A recipe on paper is no use to the chamber. The inscriber can record its arrangement and vis cost in a core.
tc.research_text.KNOWLEDGEINSCRIBER.stag:
Supplying vis is not enough. The chamber does not know how to arrange the materials or when to stop supplying it.
I have connected the workbench's recipe record to a knowledge core and tried to preserve both details. Recipes I have not yet learned gave no result. The inscriber cannot spare me the research either.

The knowledge core goes in the upper-right slot; the materials retain their workbench arrangement. When the result appeared, pressing Save added a record to the list. It remained after the core was removed and replaced.
A mistaken record can be deleted by selecting it in the list and pressing Delete. The crafting grid gives me a way to check the selection before removing the wrong neighbouring recipe.
tc.research_text.VISINTERFACE:
With the bottom of a vis relay against the interface, the network finally registered vis. Connecting the §lVis Relay Interface§r to the network before placing the relay made the connection easier to check.
Vis can enter now; the equipment still needs to know where to draw it from.The memory card recorded the interface's connection. Sneaking and right-clicking it, then right-clicking the target equipment, completed the binding.
Another Vis Relay Interface carries the connection onward. An arcane crafting terminal charges a wand, while the arcane assembly chamber keeps vis for crafting. I tested each before tidying the wiring.
tc.research_text.WIRELESSESSENTIATERMINA:
Most of the jars beside the altar are gone, but checking the remaining supply still sends me back to the essentia terminal. If an ordinary wireless terminal can read item stock, essentia readings should travel over the same connection.
I have kept the vessel controls and will try them again on a handheld terminal.

Bound to a wireless access point, the §lWireless Essentia Terminal§r gave the same readings as the fixed one. At the other workbench I could still check supplies and use vessels to deposit or withdraw.
Farther away, the connection failed. The terminal need not stay on a wall, but the access point's range still matters.

tc.research_text.ESSENTIAACCESSCARD.stag: The diffusion core left no residue on the walls of the jar as it converted the essentia. If the conversion is quick enough, perhaps a buffer vessel is unnecessary.

I fitted the core into a Basic Card and slipped it into the new slot at the end of an ME Import Bus. With the bus attached to the top of a jar, the Aer inside began to fall while the terminal recorded the same gain. I left an Aer mark in the bus and tried a jar of Ignis. This time it drew nothing. The filter does seem to hold.
An ME Export Bus reversed the flow. Once I marked the aspect I wanted, an empty jar began filling from the network and stopped when full. With several marks in place, the bus tried each in turn. I need not build a separate kind of bus for every aspect.
The Storage Bus gave a stranger result. Fitting the card made the jar's contents appear in the terminal, but its level did not move. Only when I drew a phial through the terminal did the jar lose that amount; returning it raised the level again. The essentia had stayed in the vessel all along. The network could simply reach it. Removing the card broke the connection.
The arcane crafting terminal also accepts the card. With it fitted, I can store and retrieve essentia there; without it, those entries disappear from the list. The wireless terminal behaved the same way.
tc.research_text.FLUXTRANSFERINTERFACE.s:
The nearby aura changed when I tried releasing flux from the network. Flux cannot be put in jars like essentia; the place of release needs some thought.
I paired two interfaces, one drawing vis and Ordo from the network, the other releasing the flux. I will move the outlet away from the workbench before observing further.

After pairing them with a memory card, the two §lFlux Transfer Interfaces§r can be placed separately. Flux began collecting in the outlet's chunk. Moving it farther away helps, but is not reason to stop watching.
With an ME drive and storage able to accept Vitium, some flux can condense into essentia. There is also a small chance of a spill. Spills favour the controller's location; without one, the system looks for a storage bus, then an interface.
Inspecting the arrangement will mean checking the network's equipment as well as the outlet.
tc.research_text.GACHABOX.stage.1:
The brain in a jar responded to Cognitio essentia, but repeating a trial did not repeat its result. Sometimes a thought became clear; sometimes I waited a long while and the notes went no further.
I have connected a knowledge core to the box and will record the time and yield of each turn. Enough results should tell me how useful it really is.
tc.research_text.GACHABOX.stage.2:
With the aggregator fitted above the box, right-clicking it with a brain in a jar completed the binding. The §lGacha Box§r recorded my identity; another person cannot retrieve this brain. It also needs a channel, power, and Cognitio essentia.
Each turn consumes 2 Cognitio and 500 AE, taking between 30 and 180 seconds. It accepts up to 4 Acceleration Cards. Each reduces the longest wait by 25 seconds, down to 80 seconds with all four.§lTrial Notes§r
The duration affects the yield. The current calculation gives a 75% chance of knowledge for a 30-second turn and 45% for a 180-second turn, varying linearly between them.
A successful turn makes 5 to 7 draws of 1 to 3 points each, with an equal chance of theory or observation on each draw. Acceleration shortens the wait; it does not guarantee a result.
tc.research_text.VISCONNECTIONCARD.stage:
The terminal completes the craft, but the network pays for the untyped aura. There is aura nearby; I would like it to draw that directly.
A crystal that resonates with vis may let a Basic Card sense the field around the terminal. I will fit it and compare the costs of two otherwise identical crafts.

The Basic Card infused with a vis crystal shard worked. Once installed, it drew untyped aura from nearby and the network no longer paid that part of the cost.
I fitted the §lVis Connection Card§r to a wireless arcane crafting terminal and tried again elsewhere. The source moved with me. Before crafting away from home, I should check the local aura supply too.
tc.research_text.WIRELESSARCANECRAFTINGT:
Making a replacement arcane item in the field usually means a journey back. The wireless terminal can already retrieve the materials; it only lacks a workbench and somewhere for the wand.
I have reduced the crafting terminal's arrangement, keeping the grid and wand slot. The first trial will be the same recipe, completed over a wireless connection.

Once bound to a wireless access point, the handheld terminal showed the familiar workbench. A wand in its slot works as before. So long as the signal reaches me, I need not return to the fixed terminal.
The Essentia Access Card fits too, with the same deposits and withdrawals. With a Vis Connection Card installed, crafting draws untyped aura from my surroundings rather than the place where a terminal once stood.
